keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The island 'was granted to the Hudson's Bay Company' by Letters Patent on 13 January 1849 and designated a Crown colony that day; the lease ran 1849-1859; the colonies merged in November 1866. The page gives no area; the shape is the island and the Gulf Islands. The San Juan Islands (south of the 49th parallel's channel line) were claimed by both sides from 1859 and are carried by the contest events, not the shape.

wars.name: Pig War

zones.text: the San Juan Islands, claimed by both Britain and the United States

wars.outcome: A bloodless boundary standoff over the San Juan Islands; they were 'awarded to the United States following third-party arbitration by the German Empire in 1871' (Pig War page); troops stayed on San Juan Island until 1874.
wars.note: The Pig War page infobox dates the incident June 15 - October 1859; the Vancouver Island page describes a twelve-year standoff. The war entry ends with the colony (1866); the colony of British Columbia carries the contest to 1871.

certainty.note: The island's coast is a natural border; the channel through the strait between the island and the mainland (the Oregon Treaty's 'middle of the channel') was ambiguous: 'two straits could be called the middle of the channel' and the San Juan Islands were disputed.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row. Two pages: Colony of Vancouver Island and Pig War (1859). The Oregon Treaty is cited only through the island page ('The Treaty made the 49th parallel latitude north the official border'; Pig War page: signed June 15, 1846). Not on the pages: the area, the revocation of the HBC grant by date (the page says only 'leased ... during 1849-1859'), the Pig War incident itself (15 June 1859), the 1872 award date and the withdrawal, which the Pig War page puts at 1871 (arbitration) and 1874 (troops). The HBC lease is recorded as vassal events with rupert-s-land as counterpart (a modelling choice: the company held and governed the island). Gazetteer: no Vancouver Island region, so the researcher's polygon intersects British Columbia.
